title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.39155v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents often receive access to more files, accounts, and services than a task requires. Prompt injection turns this excess access into an opportunity to redirect execution toward unrelated resources. Applying least privilege therefore requires identifying the assets needed by a task, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution. We present REALM (Required Execution Assets Linked to a Mission), an approach to identifying and maintaining a task's required assets and their permitted uses. The approach represents required assets as Dependency Graph nodes, resolves prerequisite relationships, and admits newly discovered assets through source-scoped selection. It separates discovering an asset from authorizing its use, while preserving the agent's freedom to choose its computation. translated_title: REALM：为LLM智能体识别最小任务资产
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体通常获得超出任务所需的文件、账户和服务访问权限。提示注入会将这种过剩的访问权限转变为将执行重定向到无关资源的机会。因此，应用最小权限原则需要识别任务所需的资产，包括那些身份仅在执行过程中才会显现的资产。我们提出了REALM（与任务关联的必需执行资产），这是一种识别和维护任务所需资产及其允许用途的方法。该方法将所需资产表示为依赖图节点，解析先决条件关系，并通过源范围选择接纳新发现的资产。它将资产的发现与使用授权分离开来，同时保留智能体选择其计算方式的自由。REALM构建器维护所选的授权并投影资产文件；部分API管理器暴露资源……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出REALM方法，通过依赖图识别并动态维护LLM智能体完成任务所需的最小资产集，将资产发现与使用授权分离，以实现最小权限原则并防御提示注入攻击。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes REALM, an approach that identifies and dynamically maintains the minimal set of assets required by LLM agents via dependency graphs, separating asset discovery from use authorization to enforce least privilege and defend against prompt injection attacks.
